point: Premise correction: the whole $48,000 cannot be rolled into a Roth in one year. The SECURE 2.0 529-to-Roth rollover (IRC 529(c)(3)(E), Pub. L. 117-328 section 126, distributions after December 31, 2023) is capped each year at the son's Roth limit (408A(c)(2), the section 219 maximum): the lesser of $7,500 for 2026 (IR-2025-111) and his taxable compensation, reduced by his other IRA contributions for the year (e.g. ample wages and $2,000 into his own Roth gives $5,500; $4,000 earned and $2,000 contributed gives $2,000).

Lifetime cap: $35,000 per beneficiary, all years combined (Pub 590-A), so at least $13,000 (48,000 - 35,000) can never reach the son's Roth this way, and moving the full $35,000 takes at least five tax years (7,500 x 4 = 30,000 for 2026-2029, plus 5,000 in 2030).

The Roth must be the son's own, opened by him before the transfer, and the money must move by direct trustee-to-trustee transfer into a Roth maintained for the benefit of the beneficiary; a check paid out to the family (an indirect rollover) or a parent-owned Roth fails.

Only 529 contributions made more than 5 years before the transfer, plus their earnings, qualify (Pub 970). The account opened in 2004 (about 21-22 years ago) passes the 15-year test if the son has been the beneficiary throughout, and Roth income limits do not reduce the rollover (408A(c)(3)(E)).

Moving all $48,000 in 2026 would put at least $40,500 (48,000 - 7,500) outside the rule: on the Roth side a 6% excise tax for each year the excess stays (withdrawing it with earnings by the 2026 return due date, including extensions, avoids only the 6%), and on the 529 side the earnings portion of the non-qualifying amount is taxable, generally plus the 10% additional tax.
"Tax-free" is federal only; state treatment varies, so the state tax treatment must be checked.

December is not the federal deadline: a rollover designated for 2026 can be made through April 15, 2027 (2026 Form 5498 instructions, 219(f)(3)), though whether the plan or custodian will process and code it that way varies by plan.

Steps: confirm the son's 2026 taxable compensation and that he has been the beneficiary throughout; he opens his own Roth IRA; request a direct rollover of up to $7,500 less his other 2026 IRA contributions; repeat each year until the $35,000 lifetime cap is reached; check state tax; plan for the remaining $13,000.
